name: Ananda Bazar (Jagannath Temple Mahaprasad)
signature_dish: Sankudi Mahaprasad — rice, dal, dalma and saaga eaten seated on the floor off a leaf
why_it_matters: The temple's own open-air food court in the north-east corner of the outer enclosure, where Mahaprasad cooked in the Rosa Ghara — described as the world's largest kitchen — is sold to devotees at nominal rates. Food is strictly satvik: no onion, garlic, potato, tomato or chilli. It is regularly called the biggest open-air eatery in the world, where pilgrims of every caste and background eat together on the floor.
insider_tip: Mahaprasad is freshest after roughly 2pm when the bhog cycle has been offered; come hungry but expect to sit on the floor and eat off a leaf — that is the correct way. Non-Hindus are not permitted inside the temple, so cannot reach Ananda Bazar; sealed Mahaprasad and khaja are available from shops on Grand Road instead. Carry small cash; no cards.
signature_address: Ananda Bazar, north-east corner of outer enclosure, Shree Jagannath Temple, Bada Danda, Puri, Odisha 752001

name: Wildgrass Restaurant
signature_dish: Odisha thali — dalma, chana tarkari and machha besara in a bamboo-hut garden setting
why_it_matters: Opened in 1997 to bring Odia home cooking to travellers passing through Puri, Wildgrass sits in a lush garden of bamboo huts on VIP Road, about 600m from the railway station. It is the address most consistently recommended on Tripadvisor and food guides for an authentic Odisha thali — dalma, chana tarkari, fresh local seafood — served in a dhaba-style open kitchen.
insider_tip: Ask for the full Odisha thali rather than à la carte to taste the widest spread of regional dishes in one sitting. The garden seating is pleasant in the evening; AC indoor seating exists for the summer heat. It is busy with tour groups at peak lunch — arrive before 1pm or after 8.30pm.
signature_address: VIP Road, next to Hotel Lee Garden, Dolamandap, Puri, Odisha 752001

name: Chung Wah Restaurant
signature_dish: Sichuan chicken and Hakka chow mein — Puri's oldest Chinese kitchen
why_it_matters: Started in 1975 by S. S. Lee, owner of Hotel Lee Garden, when Chinese food was unknown in Puri — it is one of the oldest Chinese restaurants in Odisha and still family-run with consistent flavours. Tripadvisor reviewers across nearly 500 ratings call it the Chinese-food landmark of the town, a reliable change of pace from temple-town thalis.
insider_tip: It is a long-standing local institution rather than a flashy place — go for the noodles and Sichuan chicken, which have stayed consistent for decades. Located on VIP Road on the way towards the beach; pair it with a stop at Wildgrass next door for two contrasting cuisines.
signature_address: VIP Road, Hotel Lee Garden, Puri, Odisha 752001

name: Pink House
signature_dish: Butter fried crab and prawn salt-and-pepper, eaten beside the sea
why_it_matters: A long-running thatched-roof seafood spot literally on the sand at the CT Road end of Puri beach — bamboo-and-clay huts that put you within earshot of the waves. Tripadvisor reviewers consistently praise the crab and prawn dishes; it is the go-to for fresh local seafood eaten with a sea view rather than inside a hotel dining room.
insider_tip: Service is slow because the kitchen is small, so order early and settle in for the setting. Crab chilli and butter fried crab are the dishes to come for; the prawn preparations are reliable. Best at sunset for the beach atmosphere. Carry cash as a backup.
signature_address: Chakratirtha Road, on the beach, Puri, Odisha 752002

name: Honey Bee Bakery & Pizzeria
signature_dish: Wood-fired pizza and fresh-baked cake on a sea-view terrace
why_it_matters: Run since 2002 by filmmaker Debabrata Tripathi on CT Road — the backpacker street where foreign travellers have come since the 1960s. It is the long-standing bakery-cafe of Puri's traveller scene, with a rooftop terrace catching a sea view and a small library shelf for book lovers. A reliable Western-food and coffee break from temple-town fare.
insider_tip: Head to the terrace upstairs for the sea view rather than the cramped ground floor. The cakes and brown bread are the strength; pizzas are decent rather than exceptional. Quiet mornings are the best time for coffee and a book.
signature_address: Chakratirtha Road, near Chakratirtha Beach, Puri, Odisha 752002

name: Wild Cafe (Tabula Rasa)
signature_dish: Breakfast spreads and coffee in a traveller-cafe setting
why_it_matters: One of the traveller cafes clustered on CT Road, the historic backpacker strip of Puri that has drawn foreign visitors since the 1960s. It serves the all-day breakfast, coffee and relaxed-pace food that the CT Road crowd looks for, away from the temple-town bustle of Grand Road.
insider_tip: CT Road has several similar cafes within walking distance — wander the strip and pick by the crowd. Mornings are the best time for breakfast and a quiet coffee before the beach. Cash and UPI both work.

name: Chanakya BNR Hotel — The Dining Car
signature_dish: Multi-cuisine dining in a colonial railway-heritage hotel
why_it_matters: The dining room of the Chanakya BNR Hotel — a colonial-era Bengal Nagpur Railway property and one of Puri's heritage landmarks. Tripadvisor ranks its dining among the top restaurants in town. It is the most comfortable hotel-grade dining option for travellers who want regional and continental food in an old-world setting.
insider_tip: The heritage building and lawns are part of the experience — come for an unhurried lunch rather than a quick bite. Non-residents can dine here; reserve ahead in peak pilgrimage season. Pricier than the CT Road cafes but the comfort and hygiene are hotel-grade.
signature_address: Chanakya BNR Hotel, Chakratirtha Road, Puri, Odisha 752002

name: Two States (Mayfair Heritage)
signature_dish: Odia and Bengali specialities plated at a beachfront resort
why_it_matters: The signature restaurant of Mayfair Heritage on Chakratirtha Road, themed around the two neighbouring cuisines of Odisha and Bengal. It is Puri's main upscale option for regional food at five-star hygiene and comfort — a contrast to the no-frills thali houses, suited to a special meal.
insider_tip: The menu deliberately blends Odia and Bengali dishes — order across both to compare. It is a resort restaurant, so prices reflect the setting; the beachfront location and service are part of what you are paying for. Reserve on weekends and in pilgrimage season.
signature_address: Mayfair Heritage, Chakratirtha Road, Puri, Odisha 752002

name: Dalma Restaurant
signature_dish: Odia thali — veg, chicken and fish thalis built around dalma
why_it_matters: A Puri thali house named after dalma, the lentil-and-vegetable stew at the heart of Odia cooking. Food guides recommend it as an easy first stop for visitors new to Odia food — veg, chicken and fish thalis at temple-town prices. It is a separate establishment from the Bhubaneswar restaurant of the same name.
insider_tip: The set thalis are the value pick — they bundle dalma, chana tarkari, rice and a side into one plate. Come for lunch when the thali spread is freshest. Cash and UPI accepted.

name: Harekrishna Veg Restaurant
signature_dish: Pure-veg thali for pilgrims near the temple
why_it_matters: A pure-vegetarian restaurant in the temple area serving pilgrims who want a simple satvik-style meal close to Jagannath Temple. It is listed on Tripadvisor among Puri's restaurants and is a practical, no-frills option for families and devotees who avoid onion-garlic food.
insider_tip: Convenient for a meal between temple darshan and Grand Road shopping. The thali is the straightforward choice; portions are generous for the price. Busiest at lunch — come slightly early for faster service.
signature_address: Grand Road / Temple area, Puri, Odisha 752001

name: Grand Road Khaja Shops (Bada Danda cluster)
signature_dish: Puri khaja — crisp, multi-layered deep-fried pastry soaked in sugar syrup
why_it_matters: Khaja — a crisp, flaky, multi-layered pastry soaked in sugar syrup — is Puri's signature sweet and part of the Jagannath Temple's chhappan bhog offering. Dozens of khaja shops line Bada Danda (Grand Road) in front of the temple. Puri khaja has been recognised internationally, including a TasteAtlas listing among the world's best sweet pastries.
insider_tip: Buy khaja fresh and still slightly warm from a busy shop on Grand Road rather than pre-packed boxes — it stays crisp only a few days. Shops near Bagala Dharmasala and Swargadwara are the established clusters. It travels well as a gift but eat it within the week.
signature_address: Bada Danda (Grand Road), in front of Jagannath Temple, Puri, Odisha 752001

name: Honey Bee Bakery — Grand Road outlet area sweets
signature_dish: Gupchup, aloo chop and ghuguni along Grand Road and the beach
why_it_matters: Grand Road and the Marine Drive beach stretch are lined with street-food carts serving Odia gupchup (puchka), aloo chop, ghuguni and dahi bara — the everyday snack food of Puri's pilgrim and beach crowds. These carts are the cheapest and most local way to eat between temple darshan and the sea.
insider_tip: Pick the busiest cart with high turnover for freshness, especially in the heat. Evening on the beach road is when the carts are fully set up. Gupchup here uses a tangier, lighter masala water than the north-Indian style. Carry small notes.
signature_address: Grand Road and Marine Drive beach stretch, Puri, Odisha 752001
